summary: Marps is an interactive web application for planning scientific field missions on Mars, focused on Jezero crater. It combines NASA imagery, terrain data, Perseverance sampling sites, and historical weather measurements in one map. Users can select scientific stops, draw routes, organize activities, and estimate travel time, reserves, and return limits. By turning planetary datasets into a practical planning experience, Marps addresses the challenge of helping future explorers make informed decisions with limited resources and communication. Offline access supports autonomy, while clear source references and uncertainty labels distinguish real observations from simulated mission assumptions.
details:
Marps connects a global Mars atlas with detailed mission planning in Jezero crater. Users can inspect imagery, geology, elevation, and slopes; explore sites studied by Perseverance; and build an itinerary from a simulated camp. The application calculates distances and time budgets, includes the return journey, and offers an optional experimental oxygen model. Plans and activity checklists are saved locally, and prepared maps remain available offline.

Its creative approach connects planetary science with the decisions an explorer must make: where to go, what to investigate, and when to return. The intended impact is to make Mars data easier to understand and support exploration planning and education.

We built Marps with React, TypeScript, Vite, OpenLayers, Tailwind CSS, and Python data preparation scripts. We considered scientific traceability, missing data, terrain resolution, accessibility, and connectivity limits. AI coding assistants supported development; scientific datasets and imagery come from credited sources. Marps is a planning prototype, not a validated navigation or life-support system.
